_comment: The synthetic corpus the unit tests run against. Every date here is a real NSE
trading day (verified against pandas_market_calendars 5.4.0), because the tests
assert on real holidays: 2026-01-26 is Republic Day and 2026-01-24/25 are a
weekend, and none of the three may ever be reported as a capture gap.
2026-01-15 is absent on purpose and is NOT a hole: NSE was shut that day for the
Maharashtra municipal corporation elections, which pandas_market_calendars 5.4.0
does not know. See NSE_ERRATA in trading_calendar.py. It mirrors the real corpus,
which has neither a file nor a manifest row for that date.
The corpus deliberately has one hole and one quarantined session:
- 2026-01-20 and 2026-01-21 are trading days with no file  -> capture gap
- 2026-02-03 has a file but the producer quarantined it     -> present, untrusted
Capture 'stops' after 2026-02-03, mirroring the real corpus's dead tail.
Checked in as text rather than as parquet + sqlite binaries on purpose: the
repository's .gitignore (owned by PR #8) ignores '*.sqlite' at any depth, so a
checked-in fixture manifest would be silently untracked and the suite would pass
here and fail on a fresh clone. Materialising both from this file also keeps the

sessions.reason: stale prices on 58% of symbols after 11:04
